title: Lemlist Pricing 2026: Every Plan and Cost Per User
summary: Lemlist pricing starts at 55€ monthly (billed annually), so you'll know the Email plan cost and 50,000 monthly email limit before deciding.
body_markdown:
## Syncing lemlist leads and replies with your stack


Once you've picked lemlist, a workflow tool can carry its leads and replies into your CRM, Slack or a spreadsheet, and it changes nothing about what lemlist charges you.


### Avoiding missed lemlist replies and lead handoffs


The failure here is usually quiet. A prospect replies, the reply sits in the sending tool, and the salesperson who owns the account finds it days later, or never. Nothing errors and no limit trips. The handoff was simply never built.


Two steps close that gap: a trigger that fires when something happens, and an action that does something with it, so the gap closes itself the moment something changes.


The canvas below shows that shape with a failed Stripe payment as the trigger and a Slack message to a channel as the action.


The run details on the left show the first step completed, and the banner at the bottom confirms the run succeeded.


Take the structure, not the payment example. Replace the trigger with a lemlist event, such as a lead replying, and keep the Slack action. Your team then sees each reply in a channel where people already look.


Point the action at a CRM record or a spreadsheet row instead and the same two steps keep your pipeline current without anyone copying data by hand, which means the hours spent on copy-paste and the typos baked into it both go away.


The canvas above is Activepieces, whose MIT-licensed core carries 746 integrations, counted from the community integrations directory of its open source monorepo on GitHub, covering the CRMs, sheets and Slack channels in question, and Alan and Funding Societies are among the teams that run Activepieces.


Before you rely on it, check on lemlist's pricing and integration pages that the event you need is exposed on your plan. A trigger you can't reach is the same silent gap again.


### When lemlist's native CRM sync is enough


If lemlist already connects natively to your CRM and does what you need, skip the workflow tool. It adds one more login, one more thing that can break, and possibly one more bill.


A native sync that covers lead creation and reply logging is enough for many teams.


When you need a step the native connection lacks, a separate tool earns its place. Examples are routing replies to different people, posting to Slack, or writing to a sheet your finance team keeps.


If your list of needs stops at "lead appears in the CRM," skip it, and keep your total to lemlist's own cost.
